# Program review: the 2026-08 campaign {#sec-program-review-2026-08}

::: {.callout-note title="What this chapter is"}
This chapter is the authoritative synthesis of the research program as of
2026-08-19. It supersedes the earlier "future directions" chapter (whose open
questions have all since been measured) and compresses roughly sixty
preregistered training runs, four adversarial probes, and three architecture
generations into the tables and verdicts a reviewer actually needs. Every
number is computed live from the committed reduction artifacts in
`results/`, and every claim links to the dated lab-notebook entry
(@sec-notebook) where it was preregistered and read out.
:::

## The one-paragraph verdict

The program set out to build a boundary-driven-PDE surrogate whose
generalization comes from **declared physical structure** rather than data
coverage. After a falsification campaign against the strongest available
incumbent (GeoTransolver, a soft-slice global-attention architecture), the
honest verdict is a *decomposition*: *accuracy* at industrial scale comes
from normalized global routing and rich features, and the incumbent had it;
*pose robustness* comes from exact equivariance, the incumbent measurably
lacks it, and buying it with data augmentation costs 1.8--1.9$\times$
accuracy where our contracts provide it free; *cross-family transfer* comes
from training-data diversity, not from any architecture we tested; and
*query-independence* — the ability to evaluate the surrogate anywhere without
the answer depending on which other points are sampled — trades directly
against accuracy in every design we built. The program's product is
`MeshTransformer2` (MT2): the incumbent's routing wrapped in exact contracts
at the network's edges, within 10--18% of the incumbent's in-family accuracy
at equal-or-lower cost, exactly pose-robust, and transferring at parity when
trained on two families.

## The frozen instrument {#sec-review-instrument}

Every comparison in this chapter runs on one instrument, frozen on
2026-08-04 and never widened retroactively: DrivAerML surface pressure at
10,000-cell sampling (in-family), a five-resolution sweep (2.5k--40k cells),
zero-shot evaluation on two held-out SHIFT-SUV vehicle families (estate and
fastback, normalized pressure $L_2$ from the fleet-comparable
`metrics.jsonl` pathway), and — added mid-campaign as adversarial probes —
a full random-yaw rotation orbit (P1), a drive-amplitude scaling ladder
(P2), a 10:1 spatially-biased sampling density with exact
Horvitz--Thompson weights (P3), and a shared-prefix companion-set stability
test (P4). Training protocol is identical for every arm ever compared: 500
epochs, batch 1, lr $3\times10^{-3}$ StepLR, bfloat16, no augmentation
unless the augmentation *is* the arm, four-GPU single-node DDP on identical
hardware. A two-point learning-rate parity check ran for both architectures;
it moves the headline gap from 1.18$\times$ to 1.10$\times$ in MT2's favor
and is reported wherever it matters.

## The frontier, in one table {#sec-review-frontier}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-frontier
#| output: asis
#| code-fold: true
import json
from pathlib import Path

R = Path("..") / "results" / "mixedres_training_2026-07-31" / "sweep"
mega = json.load(open(R / "mega_reduction.json"))
round3 = json.load(open(R / "round3_reduction.json"))
v3c = json.load(open(R / "mt2_v3c_reduction.json"))

def mean(vals):
    return sum(vals) / len(vals)

gt10 = mean([round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["sweep_metrics"]["10000"]["mean"]
             for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gt_zs = mean([round3[f"gt_fixed_seed{s}"]["smoke_estate"]["mean"]
              for s in (42, 43, 44)])

rot_in = mean([mega[f"gt_rotaug_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43)])
rot_zs = mean([mega[f"gt_rotaug_seed{s}"]["estate"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43)])

v3c_in = mean(
    [v3c[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["sweep"]["10000"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)]
    + [mega[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (45, 46)]
)
v3c_zs = mean([v3c[f"mt2_v3c_seed{s}"]["smoke_estate"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])

mt2m_in = mean([mega[f"mt2_multi_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
mt2m_zs = mean([mega[f"mt2_multi_seed{s}"]["fastback"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gtm_in = mean([mega[f"gt_multi_seed{s}"]["in10k"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])
gtm_zs = mean([mega[f"gt_multi_seed{s}"]["fastback"]["mean"] for s in (42, 43, 44)])

rows = [
    ("GeoTransolver 9M", 1.0, gt_zs, "3.6x", "26-32x broken", "4.6 GB",
     "incumbent reference"),
    ("GT + rotation aug.", rot_in / gt10, rot_zs, "--", "closed (1.00)",
     "4.6 GB", "the augmentation price"),
    ("MT2-v3c (8.6M)", v3c_in / gt10, v3c_zs, "13-14x", "exact (1.00)",
     "5.9 GB", "canonical single-family MT2"),
    ("GT multi-family", gtm_in / gt10, gtm_zs, "--", "26-32x broken",
     "4.6 GB", "zero-shot on HELD-OUT family"),
    ("MT2 multi-family", mt2m_in / gt10, mt2m_zs, "--", "exact (1.00)",
     "5.9 GB", "zero-shot on HELD-OUT family"),
]
out = ("| configuration | in-family (xGT) | zero-shot | density (P3) "
       "| rotation (P1) | peak VRAM | note |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
for (n, i, z, d, r_, m, note) in rows:
    out += f"| {n} | {i:.2f}x | {z:.2f} | {d} | {r_} | {m} | {note} |\n"
print(out)
print(f": The frontier on the frozen instrument. In-family is normalized "
      f"pressure $L_2$ at 10k cells relative to the GeoTransolver reference "
      f"({gt10:.4f}); zero-shot is the mean normalized pressure $L_2$ on a "
      f"held-out vehicle family (estate for single-family rows, fastback "
      f"for the multi-family rows; 1.0 is mean-predictor level). Sources: "
      f"mega_reduction.json, round3_reduction.json, mt2_v3c_reduction.json.")
```

Three facts to read off the table before any narrative. First, **the
augmentation price**: closing GeoTransolver's rotation hole with the classic
data-augmentation remedy costs it most of its accuracy lead —
1.8--1.9$\times$ in-family — while MT2's exact equivariance is free by
construction; at equal pose-robustness the structured model is the
*more* accurate one by roughly 1.6$\times$. Second, **transfer belongs to
data**: one additional training family moves zero-shot error on a genuinely
held-out family from mean-predictor level to 0.11--0.13 for *both*
architectures — a $\sim$7$\times$ improvement that dwarfs every
architectural intervention this program ever measured against that axis.
Third, **the remaining accuracy gap is small and tuning-sensitive**: 1.18×
at the frozen learning rate, 1.10× when each architecture uses its
preferred rate.

## How we got here: the campaign in five verdicts {#sec-review-arc}

**1. The old architecture's defects were real, and three closed at root
cause** (@sec-nb-model-quality-agenda ff.). Resolution collapse was a
quadrature-bookkeeping error, cured by measure-consistent
Horvitz--Thompson weighting (@sec-nb-mixedres-verdict). Foreign-family
detonation was the nonlinear read-in's implicit drive degree, removed
exactly by declaring degree one (@sec-nb-bounded-stage1-verdict). Seed
instability collapsed from 2491$\times$ to order-1.3$\times$ as a
byproduct. These closures are the program's clearest demonstrations that
mechanism-first debugging beats remedy-first patching.

**2. The incumbent comparison was re-anchored honestly and the incumbent
won the measured axes** (@sec-nb-incumbent-stage0-verdict,
@sec-nb-defect4-synthesis). At every resource budget tested,
GeoTransolver dominated in-family accuracy, zero-shot transfer, density
robustness, and training cost — including a resource re-framing
(@sec-nb-resource-accounting) that showed the original matched-*parameter*
comparison had flattered our side. The synthesis recommended inverting the
program: structure the winner rather than accelerate the loser.

**3. The probes made the benchmark's blind spots measurable**
(@sec-nb-contract-probes-synthesis). Rotation: the incumbent loses
26--32$\times$ off-pose — every number it posts carries an implicit "in
the dataset's canonical pose." Amplitude: its output is drive-amplitude
*blind* (layer normalization saturates scale), while the declared-degree
contract measures exactly 1.0000. Density: geometry-adaptive statistics
pay a variance-bounded tax no weighting scheme removes; the measure
contract halves the damage but cannot zero it.

**4. MT2 was built in eleven preregistered iterations, most of which
failed informatively** (@sec-nb-mt2-charter through
@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict). The thesis — the incumbent's routing on
exclusively invariant features, contracts paid once at the network edges —
was refuted at v0 (non-separating invariants), survived at v0b, shed its
global frames entirely at v2 on Peter's correction that no canonical frame
exists in the physics, and closed its in-family gap by featurization alone
(3.08$\times \to$ 1.15$\times$; capacity was flat at every rung tested).
The accuracy--robustness trade that emerged was then shown to be a
*single-family-training artifact*, dissolved by data diversity rather than
architecture.

**5. Query-independence was priced, and the price is the finding**
(@sec-nb-v5-line-verdict). Three passive-decoder designs either collapsed
in training or, once the collapse was fixed by a local token readout,
converged 2.7$\times$ worse in-family while achieving the best density
robustness of any variant. Conclusion, now measured rather than argued:
**in this design family, accuracy and query-interaction are entangled** —
the query-side token stream is where the accuracy comes from, which is
also precisely why the accurate models carry companion-set sensitivity
(2% for the incumbent, 6.8% for MT2-v3c on the P4 probe). A deployable
surrogate can have exact evaluate-anywhere semantics at 3.9$\times$ the
error, or near-incumbent accuracy with single-digit-percent sensitivity;
it cannot currently have both.

## What this does not solve {#sec-review-honesty}

The claims above are scoped by construction, and the scoping is part of
the result. Everything rests on two automotive dataset families plus a
harder third (high-lift) in flight; no volume fields; no varying boundary
conditions — the typed-BC ingestion that distinguishes the GLOBE lineage
is designed but unbuilt *because no current benchmark can measure it*, and
building unmeasurable structure is how this program wasted its first week.
Density robustness is scoped at $\sim$13$\times$ under a 10:1 sampling
bias (variance-floored). Both architectures misbehave at scale extremes
under the frozen learning rate (seed-conditioned detonations at 11M for
the old architecture; a turned frontier at 564M for the incumbent), so
no "scales to very large runs" claim is made by either side. And the
irreducible-error question — whether the 1.10$\times$ residual gap is
architecture or the dataset's time-averaging noise floor — is exactly
what the in-flight high-lift wave (@sec-nb-highlift-prereg) exists to
answer.

## Roads from here {#sec-review-roads}

In recommended order: (1) a scoped experimental release of MT2-v3c/v4 —
"exactly pose-robust surface aero surrogate at incumbent-class accuracy
and cost," with the augmentation pricing as its headline evidence and the
entanglement finding as its stated limitation; (2) the high-lift verdict,
which either extends the claim to harder physics or bounds it; (3) the
upstream PR series for the engineering bycatch (rank-failure barrier,
distributed-timeout knob, degenerate-cell guards, measure machinery — all
verified still absent upstream); (4) a BC-varying benchmark *before* any
typed-BC architecture work; and (5) the shelved query-independence line,
revisited only with the two untried levers (auxiliary encoder supervision,
warm-starting) and only if a deployment actually demands
evaluate-anywhere semantics at the measured price.
